2607.23237.title: Context-Aware Concept Distillation for Trustworthy Flood Prediction
2607.23237.paper_summary: Effective flood risk management relies on accurate forecasting, yet the "black box" nature of stateof-the-art Deep Learning models creates a barrier to trust and accountability in high-stakes public safety decisions. While existing Explainable AI (XAI) methods offer local attributions, they fail to provide the verifiable, operationally meaningful causal narratives required by disaster response authorities. To address this societal challenge, we propose Context-Aware Concept Distillation (CACD), a framework developed in collaboration with domain experts to distill opaque LSTMs into interpretable, hydrology-aware surrogate models. We introduce an unsupervised pipeline to discover a "Hydrological Language" and a Residual Hypernetwork that dynamically modulates these concepts based on static basin characteristics. Evaluated on 5,203 basins globally, our model achieves high fidelity (Median NSE 0.70), significantly outperforming black-box baselines (e.g., Multi Layer Perceptrons) on unseen future data. By demonstrating that human-interpretable concepts are sufficient to reconstruct flood dynamics, this work balances AI accuracy with the transparency required for responsible environmental decision-making.
2607.23237.paper_summary_zh: 有效的洪水風險管理依賴於準確的預測，然而最先進的深度學習模型的「黑箱」特性在高風險公共安全決策中造成了信任和問責的障礙。雖然現有的可解釋人工智慧（XAI）方法提供了局部歸因，但它們未能提供災害應對機構所需的可驗證、操作上有意義的因果敘事。為了解決這一社會挑戰，我們提出了上下文感知概念蒸餾（CACD），這是一個與領域專家合作開發的框架，用於將不透明的長短期記憶網絡（LSTMs）蒸餾成可解釋的、具有水文意識的替代模型。我們引入了一個無監督的流程來發現「水文語言」，以及一個殘差超網絡，該網絡根據靜態流域特徵動態調節這些概念。在全球5,203個流域上進行評估，我們的模型達到了高保真度（中位數NSE 0.70），在未見的未來數據上顯著超越了黑箱基準（例如，多層感知器）。通過證明人類可解釋的概念足以重建洪水動態，這項工作在AI準確性與負責任的環境決策所需的透明度之間取得了平衡。
